task.title: Implement global World of Warcraft-inspired crowd-control diminishing returns for Path of the Shaman
task.instruction: Implement the working JASS/vJASS library, not merely a design proposal. Inspect the project and reference implementations first, then create the requested library with minimal integration burden.

project.name: Path of the Shaman
project.target_runtime: Warcraft III version used by the existing PotS project; verify before selecting patch-specific natives

read_first.purpose: Understand current stun prevention, event interception, targeted/AoE/passive handling, dummy stuns, and restoration semantics; use as reference, not a scope limit.
Reuse safe ideas for per-target category stages, reset windows, buff checks, and event handling; critically review all assumptions and known limitations.
Inspect nearby PotS libraries, import/build conventions, reusable utility libraries, and any available object-data or custom-ability sources.

scope_and_constraints.dependency_policy: Prefer existing project-compatible dependencies. Do not introduce a new required third-party dependency without necessity and documentation.
scope_and_constraints.manual_per_ability_registration: not acceptable as the primary integration mechanism
scope_and_constraints.compilation: Must compile under the actual PotS JASS/vJASS toolchain; do not assume that a different compiler or language is available.
scope_and_constraints.external_generated_metadata: May be proposed as an optional future solution, but do not write new companion files unless essential and explicitly justified in the final report.

global_operation.goal: Automatically apply category-shared diminishing returns to as many real crowd-control effects in the map as the engine can reliably observe and modify, including standard and custom abilities.
global_operation.coverage_requirement: Do not stop at the two abilities handled by the existing StunGuard or the small manual registry in the draft.

categories.label: Roots
examples: Frost Nova (only if its actual effect is a root)
Ice Trap (only if its implementation applies a root)

classification_rules: All abilities and effects assigned to the same category share one diminishing-returns state for each target.
Each category maintains its own independent state for each target.
Categorize the actual crowd-control effect, not the display name of the ability.
The examples are semantic guidance, not proof that the PotS map contains these abilities or that they have the stated effect.
For abilities applying multiple distinct crowd-control effects, classify and handle each qualifying effect separately when technically possible.
Do not apply DR to ordinary slows, damage-over-time, utility debuffs, or unrelated buffs.
Do not add knockback, disarm, or taunt categories unless explicitly requested later.

dr_model.design_reference: World of Warcraft-style crowd-control diminishing returns, adapted for PotS
dr_model.stage_after_third_success: Immune to further effects in the same category until the reset window expires.
dr_model.window_anchor: Actual end of the last successfully applied qualifying crowd-control effect, not its cast start.
dr_model.reset_rule: After an uninterrupted 18-second period with no active successful crowd-control effect from that category on the target, the next successful application starts at 100% duration.
dr_model.natural_expiry_and_early_removal: Track effect ending as accurately as feasible; dispel, cancellation, death, or premature expiry must not leave an incorrect persistent stage or timer.
dr_model.overlap_and_refresh_semantics: Define deterministic handling of overlapping or refreshed effects. Avoid allowing a reduced cast to extend an existing effect contrary to DR, or a later cast to change the recorded expiration incorrectly.
dr_model.base_duration: Use the ability's effective applicable duration before DR, taking ability level and target-specific hero/normal/resistant duration rules into account.
dr_model.damage_and_other_spell_effects: Preserve non-CC spell behavior, including damage, costs, cooldowns, visuals, and unrelated secondary effects unless the selected enforcement approach makes this impossible; clearly document any such limitation.
dr_model.scope: Apply to all relevant targets that can receive these effects in PotS unless an existing design constraint requires an explicit exclusion; do not assume WoW's PvP-only scope applies to PotS.

ability_delivery_modes: passive attack-proc stuns or other passive crowd control
triggered or dummy-unit abilities where safely detectable
custom Object Editor abilities based on standard templates
multi-target effects where different victims have different current DR stages

preferred_strategy: Inspect the map's accessible object data and ability definitions to infer which abilities apply which buff/effect and its category, without asking the map author to write RegisterAbility calls.
Use reliable native spell/unit events for candidate application events and targeted follow-up checks only when necessary.
Use known Warcraft III buff rawcodes, actual applied buff presence, ability effects, and existing PotS mechanisms where they provide trustworthy classification and confirmation.
Keep lookup metadata inside DiminishingReturns.j if automatic source analysis can generate it without requiring ongoing manual registration.

For effects with no cast event (for example passive procs), seek an existing proc/damage integration point or another reliable narrow observation method; count the stage only when an effect truly lands.
automatic_detection.buff_preference: Lean heavily on buff/effect evidence when it improves correctness, including distinguishing cast attempts from successful applications.
automatic_detection.critical_engine_limitation: Standard Warcraft III JASS does not provide a universal native callback enumerating every arbitrary buff addition together with its category, original duration, and caster. Do not claim magical discovery of all unknown custom buffs or arbitrary triggered effects.
automatic_detection.fallback_policy: If full zero-configuration global coverage is impossible, implement the widest provably correct automatic subset and explicitly report uncovered ability families, reasons, and the smallest optional integration seam needed for full coverage.
automatic_detection.false_positive_policy: Do not guess a crowd-control category or advance DR from an attack, a cast start, or an unknown buff alone.

application_engine.correct_timing: Apply DR before the engine creates the final CC duration, or use a validated mechanism that adjusts the actual resulting CC without side effects. Simple post-cast stage bookkeeping without real duration enforcement is insufficient.
application_engine.field_mutation_safety: If changing per-unit ability instance level fields via BlzSetAbilityRealLevelField, snapshot exact original values and restore on all exit paths; verify compatibility and isolate concurrent casts from the same caster.
application_engine.area_of_effect_safety: Per-target stages may differ in one AoE cast; never shorten or suppress an entire AoE solely because one target has a higher DR stage. Use a verified per-target mechanism or explicitly document the unavoidable limitation.
application_engine.passive_proc_safety: Do not count a normal attack as a successful Bash proc; only a confirmed applied stun should alter state.
application_engine.no_unwanted_zero_duration_interrupts: Check project game constants such as CanInterruptByZeroDurationBuffs when using suppression or dummy techniques.
application_engine.legacy_interactions: Examine StunGuard's separate stun suppression and dummy replacement. Avoid double-processing if both libraries are installed. Do not silently change StunGuard's existing behavior or remove it.
application_engine.engine_compatibility: Validate natives, dummy rawcodes, special buff handling, spell event timing, and integer level indexing against the project's Warcraft III version.

minimal_optional_functions: query target/category reset status or remaining window
enable or disable library for debugging/testing
public_api.design_rule: Expose a small stable API if useful, but normal gameplay must not require any per-ability registration calls. Use the project's naming and encapsulation conventions.

performance.goal: No perceptible gameplay lag, including dense combat and large AoE encounters.
avoid: global per-frame scanning of all units and all possible buffs
creating one persistent timer or trigger per unit per category without a justified bound
large repeated enumerations of the entire map
repeated object-data lookups or buff scans for irrelevant events
unnecessary dummy creation in hot paths
prefer: single shared clock or bounded sparse scheduling
early filtering and cached static metadata
reuse and cleanup of temporary groups, timers, and handles
checking only units plausibly affected by a triggering spell or proc
performance.proof: Measure or at least instrument typical combat and stress cases; do not simply assert the implementation is lag-free.

quality: Follow established PotS JASS/vJASS structure, naming, formatting, and initialization patterns.
Keep algorithms deterministic, easy to audit, and independent of frame-rate fluctuations where possible.
Do not use deprecated or unverified functions where a supported equivalent exists.
Document any assumptions about buffs, disabled abilities, immunity, targets, and available object data directly in the library.
Prefer maintainable code over clever heuristics that can break unrelated abilities.

implementation_workflow.name: Audit existing PotS behavior
required_actions: Inspect both referenced JASS implementations and the build/import conventions.
Identify legacy StunGuard interactions and likely shared stun buffs or dummy abilities.

implementation_workflow.name: Determine provable automatic coverage
required_actions: Inspect available ability and buff object data and locate reusable event/proc systems.
Build an internal classification approach that does not impose manual calls at each spell site.
Distinguish what can be detected from what requires explicit instrumentation.

implementation_workflow.name: Implement global DR engine
required_actions: Implement separate target-category stages and accurate reset windows.
Implement real duration reduction or immunity enforcement for supported effects.
Handle targeted, AoE, passive, and triggered effects to the extent proven safe.
Minimize work and allocations in combat hot paths.

implementation_workflow.name: Verify behavior and integration
required_actions: Run JASS/vJASS compilation with the project's actual toolchain where accessible.
Run focused tests and regression checks; if in-game tests cannot be run, identify them as unverified instead of claiming success.
Review leaks, early dispels, unit reuse, AoE stage differences, and interaction with StunGuard.

implementation_workflow.name: Report implementation honestly
required_actions: Report created file, integration requirement, and tests performed.
List automatically supported CC families and any unsupported cases, with precise reasons.
Describe any conflict with StunGuard and how to avoid loading both handlers concurrently.
Do not modify unrelated project files to conceal limitations.

acceptance_tests.description: First confirmed root on a fresh target lasts 100% of its actual base duration.
Second confirmed root from a different root ability inside the active window lasts 50%.
Third confirmed root lasts 25%; fourth and later attempts have 0% root duration until reset.
Stun, root, incapacitate, disorient, and silence stages remain independent for the same target.
Two targets hit by one AoE receive durations according to their respective stage; immune targets do not suppress the effect on eligible targets.
Reset occurs 18 seconds after the last successful CC ends; a cast that fails, misses, or is resisted does not advance the stage.
An immune attempt neither advances DR nor shifts the reset time.
Early dispel or cancellation, overlapping effects, and refreshes do not corrupt active duration or reset timing.
Passive Bash only counts on a successful stun proc, not on every attack or damage event.
Storm Bolt maintains its damage and visuals while its stun is diminished.
The AoE and dummy implementation does not modify other units' ability fields or leave modified ability duration fields behind after interruption.
No duplicate DR processing or hidden conflict occurs when evaluating compatibility with the existing StunGuard; explicitly require disabling one handler if coexistence is unsafe.
Library compiles with the actual PotS toolchain and uses valid target-version JASS natives.
Repeated combat, many targets, and long play sessions do not cause runaway handles, timers, retained state, or perceptible frame drops.
The coverage report distinguishes native, custom, and non-observable triggered CC; no undocumented assumption of universal coverage.

required_final_report: Summary of implementation and key architectural decisions
How the new library is initialized or loaded using existing project workflow
Which CC types and ability-delivery modes are automatically covered
Exact limitations and any minimal integration actions still needed
Compatibility and conflict assessment with StunGuard.j
Compilation and runtime test results, with failures or unavailable tests clearly identified
do_not_just_produce: a manually curated RegisterAbility list presented as universal automatic detection
a system that tracks stage but does not actually reduce or prevent CC duration

references.topic: WoW DR stages, reset timing, category behavior
User-specified categories and example ability lists; historical examples, not a required exact expansion snapshot
Buff-system architecture patterns and explicit buff event abstraction
Warcraft III native for changing ability duration fields and compatibility cautions
PotS reference implementations and local project conventions
